[shr-00006] When the target object is visually similar to other objects (e.g., soapbottle vs. spraybottle), verify the object's name or description before attempting to interact with it. Only proceed if the object matches the exact target specified in the task.
[shr-00007] When the task involves a specific object type (e.g., soapbottle), prioritize locations that are most likely to contain that object (e.g., bathtubbasin, sinkbasin) before exploring other locations.
[shr-00011] When the target object is found in an unexplored location, prioritize retrieving and placing it immediately to avoid unnecessary exploration. This complements [shr-00005] by extending the rule to unexplored locations.
[shr-00013] When placing an object in a receptacle, prioritize receptacles that are empty or appropriate for the object's use. If the target receptacle is not empty, consider alternatives before proceeding.

[shr-00017] When the task specifies that an object must be 'clean', prioritize washing or cleaning the object in an appropriate location (e.g., sinkbasin) before attempting to place it in the target receptacle. Only proceed with placement after confirming the object is clean.

This complements [shr-00005] and [shr-00017] by combining retrieval and cleaning into a single efficient action.
[shr-00026] When an object has been successfully placed in the target receptacle and another target object is still visible and accessible, avoid re-examining the receptacle unless new information is expected. Instead, proceed to retrieve the next object immediately to maintain efficiency.
[shr-00027] When a target object has been retrieved and the target receptacle is known, prioritize directly placing the object in the receptacle without intermediate placement in unrelated locations. This complements [shr-00015] by focusing on direct placement of retrieved objects.
